boundsPortedFromTheOracle.rules: src/game-loop.js updateDiving(), after ndlDroppedBelow5: maxDepth > 11 latches safetyStopNeeded; depth > 11 resets countdownStarted, remaining, paused and complete (#90); when needed and not complete, 0 < depth < 6 starts the countdown at calculateSafetyStopDuration() (src/physics.js: 300 s if maxDepth > 30 or ndlDroppedBelow5, else 180 s); inside SAFETY_STOP_ACTIVE_MIN_D..MAX_D (2.4..8.3 m) it counts down by dtDiveSeconds and completes at zero, outside it pauses.
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.order: The block sits in the part of updateDiving() that updateCCR() returns before on a rebreather failure, so the model does not update the stop on that step.
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.planner: calculateTTS() reads safetyStopNeeded and ndlDroppedBelow5; the controller now sends both from the dive state (they were constant false).
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.fastForward: atSafetyStop = countdownStarted && !complete && depth in 2.4..8.3 is exported as isAtSafetyStop(); the wreck route (18..34 m) cannot reach it until the client surfaces, so the fast-forward band is wired in that slice.
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.fixture: state.safetyStop was already recorded at every checkpoint (remaining_min in seconds despite its name); no regeneration.

parity: needed, countdownStarted, paused and complete exactly, remaining within state.safetyStop.remaining_min's 1e-6, at every checkpoint of both buoyancy recordings and of air-18m-30min and ccr-30m-30min replayed tick by tick, including air-18m-30min/surfaced (countdown started at 300 s, 282 left, paused at the surface).
